headline_hook: Google and Microsoft Ship Cybersecurity Models as Anthropic Draws the Line on Open Weights
preview_topics: Simon Willison's frontier model decision guide

pick_of_the_day.thesis: The real story isn't Anthropic's open-weights position — it's that five competing labs quietly agreed on a shared jailbreak severity scoring standard, which tells us the industry's safety coordination is outpacing its safety theater and could give us the CVSS equivalent for model failures.

model_literacy.relevance: Both Google (Flash Cyber) and Microsoft (MAI-Cyber-1-Flash) shipped purpose-built cybersecurity models today rather than fine-tuning or prompting general models — understanding when to train a domain specialist versus adapt a generalist is the architectural decision every enterprise AI team will face as this pattern spreads beyond security.

items.title: Google Drops Three Gemini Models — Including Its First Cybersecurity Specialist
items.angle: A triple launch that buries the lede: Flash 3.6 and Flash-Lite are iterative, but Flash Cyber signals Google sees security as a model vertical worth owning.
items.key_fact: Three simultaneous releases: Gemini 3.6 Flash, 3.5 Flash-Lite, and 3.5 Flash Cyber

items.title: Microsoft Answers Google's Cyber Model With MAI-Cyber-1-Flash Inside MDASH
items.angle: Same-day as Google's Flash Cyber, Microsoft ships its own security-specialist model directly into its security dashboard — the cybersecurity model race is officially on.
items.key_fact: MAI-Cyber-1-Flash integrated directly into Microsoft's MDASH security dashboard

items.title: Anthropic Publishes Its Open-Weights Stance — With a Cross-Industry Jailbreak Severity Framework
items.angle: The position paper matters less than the appendix: Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Anthropic co-developed a jailbreak severity scoring standard that could become the industry's CVSS for model safety.
items.key_fact: Cross-industry jailbreak severity scoring framework co-developed with Amazon, Microsoft, Google, and Glasswing partners

items.title: Cognizant Goes Deeper on Claude for Enterprise Deployments
items.angle: A giant systems integrator expanding its Claude integration means Anthropic's enterprise distribution story just got more concrete.
items.key_fact: Cognizant is one of the world's largest IT services firms with massive enterprise reach

items.title: MIT Tech Review: The Hugging Face Attack Wasn't 'Unprecedented' — We've Been Here Before
items.angle: A sharp counter-narrative to OpenAI's framing — the real gap isn't technical containment but institutional memory of past failures.
items.key_fact: Documents prior containment failures the industry has systematically downplayed

items.title: Simon Willison's Opinionated Guide to Picking the Right AI for the Job
items.angle: With Opus 5, Gemini 3.6, Kimi K3, and Fable all landing in the same window, a practical decision framework is exactly the signal-to-noise filter developers need.
items.key_fact: Task-type-based decision framework across current frontier models

items.title: NVIDIA's Cosmos World Model Goes Into the Operating Room
items.angle: Foundation-model-powered simulation moves from tech demos to safety-critical surgical robotics — generative world models are production-ready for high-stakes domains.
items.key_fact: Real-time generative simulation for surgical robot training and planning

quick_links.angle: Not a single god-model but coordinated agent networks as the practical path
